hints.content:
To measure slope, we pick any two points on the line. Then we look at the horizontal and vertical distances between those points.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. A graph of a line intersects the points one, negative three, and three, zero. There is a horizontal dotted segment from one, negative three to three, negative three that is labeled two. There is a vertical dotted segment from three, negative three to three, zero that is labeled three.

hints.content:
Going from the point on the left to the point on the right, the change in $y$ is $\purpleD 3$, and the change in $x$ is $\redD 2$.

$\text{Slope}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\text{rise}}}{\redD{\text{run}}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\Delta y}}{\redD{\Delta x}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{3}}{\redD{2}}$
The slope of the line is $\dfrac{3}{2}$.
